meta.title: Einstein Math
meta.subtitle: Cosmic Adventures in Numbers — Einstein teaches, you explore!

ages-5-6.label: Ages 5–6
ages-5-6.blurb: Counting & teens, compose/decompose, add/sub, time & coins, stories, patterns, data & 3D shapes — ~29 playable lessons.

units.title: Counting Adventures
units.description: Count, compare, and make friends with numbers!

units.title: Add & Take Away
units.description: Put together and take apart — within 20!

units.title: Measure & Time
units.description: Compare lengths, tell time to the hour, and meet coins!

units.title: Story Math
units.description: Add and take-away adventures in little stories!

units.title: Pattern Power
units.description: Spot patterns and skip-count by 2s and 5s!

units.title: Shape Squad
units.description: Circles, squares, triangles — meet the shape heroes!

units.title: Data Detectives
units.description: Tally marks, pictographs, and simple counts

diagnostic.title: Little Cosmic Warm-Up
diagnostic.einsteinIntro: Hi, explorer! Let's play a quick number game across counting, stories, time, and shapes. No worries — just for fun!

questions.prompt: A cube has how many faces?
Half past means the long hand is on…
9 cats, 6 dogs. How many more cats?

k-count-to-20.title: Count to 20
k-count-to-20.einsteinIntro: Numbers are like a parade! Let's march from 1 all the way to 20 — POW!

panels.speech: Start at 1… then 2, 3, 4… each number is ONE more than the last!
After 10 comes 11, 12… all the way to 20. Twenty is two groups of ten!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
steps: Last number you say is how many!

practice.prompt: How many fingers on TWO hands?
What number comes after 14? (just the number)

practice.hint: Bigger numbers come later when we count.

k-compare-small.title: Bigger & Smaller
k-compare-small.einsteinIntro: Which pile is bigger? We compare numbers like comic heroes comparing power levels!

panels.speech: Look at 4 and 7. Count up from 4… you pass 5, 6, then hit 7. So 7 is MORE!
The crocodile mouth > always eats the BIGGER number. 8 > 3!

practice.hint: Less means smaller — earlier when counting.

practice.prompt: Which is bigger, 10 or 2? Type the bigger number.

k-add-within-10.title: Add Within 10
k-add-within-10.einsteinIntro: Adding means putting amounts together — like stacking cosmic blocks!

panels.speech: 3 + 2 means start with 3, then hop 2 more: 4, 5. Answer: 5!
Friends of 10: 6 + 4 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10. Superhero pairs!

practice.prompt: You have 3 stickers and get 3 more. How many?

k-sub-within-10.title: Take Away Within 10
k-sub-within-10.einsteinIntro: Taking away is subtraction — like stars zooming off the page!

panels.speech: 8 − 3 means start with 8, hop BACK 3: 7, 6, 5. Left with 5!
Think: what do I ADD to the small number to get the big one? That's the answer!

practice.prompt: You had 8 cookies and ate 3. How many left?

k-add-within-20.title: Add Within 20
k-add-within-20.einsteinIntro: Now we blast past 10! Same idea — put together and count on.

panels.speech: 9 + 5: make a ten first! 9 needs 1 more to make 10, then 4 left → 14!
Or just count on: start at 9… 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. Same POW answer!

k-shapes-intro.title: Meet the Shapes
k-shapes-intro.einsteinIntro: Shapes are the building blocks of the comic world! Circles, squares, triangles — assemble!

panels.speech: A circle is round like a planet — no corners! A square has 4 equal sides.
A triangle has 3 sides. A rectangle has 4 sides — opposite sides match!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: How many sides does a square have?

practice.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?
Which shape is round with no corners?
practice.hint: Think of a ball or planet.

practice.prompt: A square has how many equal sides?
How many corners does a rectangle have? (number)

k-teen-numbers.title: Teen Numbers (11–19)
k-teen-numbers.einsteinIntro: Teen numbers are TEN plus some ones — like secret codes from 11 to 19!

panels.speech: Eleven is 10 + 1. Twelve is 10 + 2. Hear the pattern?
Thirteen, fourteen… all the way to nineteen = 10 + 9. POW!

k-compose-10.title: Friends of 10
k-compose-10.einsteinIntro: Numbers that make 10 are best friends! Let's find every pair — ZOOM!

panels.speech: 6 + 4 = 10. 7 + 3 = 10. They hug to make a perfect ten!
If you know one friend, you know the other. 8 needs 2!

k-length-compare.title: Longer & Shorter
k-length-compare.einsteinIntro: Which pencil is longer? Which crayon is shorter? Measurement is comparing!

panels.speech: Put objects side by side. The one that sticks out farther is LONGER!
Shorter means less length. Same length means they match — SNAP!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: A snake is longer than a worm.
steps: Line them up at one end

practice.prompt: A bus is ______ than a bike.
practice.feedbackWrong: A bus is longer than a bike.

practice.prompt: If two ribbons match end to end, they are…
Which is shorter: a paperclip or a meter stick?
How many ends do you line up to compare length? (number)

quickCheck.prompt: A mouse is ______ than an elephant.

k-time-hour.title: Time to the Hour
k-time-hour.einsteinIntro: Clocks are cosmic circles! When the big hand points to 12, we say o'clock!

panels.speech: The SHORT hand tells the hour. The LONG hand on 12 means o'clock!
Short hand on 3 + long on 12 → 3 o'clock. Easy as relativity!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: What time is short hand on 5, long on 12?

practice.prompt: When the long hand is on 12, we say…
Short hand on 2, long on 12. Time?
Short hand on 7, long on 12. What hour? (just the number)

practice.feedbackWrong: The short hand shows the hour.

quickCheck.prompt: 3 o'clock means the long hand is on…
Short hand on 9, long on 12. Hour?

k-coins-intro.title: Meet the Coins
k-coins-intro.einsteinIntro: Coins are tiny treasure! Penny, nickel, dime, quarter — let's meet them!

panels.speech: A penny is 1¢. A nickel is 5¢. A dime is 10¢. A quarter is 25¢!
5 pennies = 1 nickel. 2 nickels = 1 dime. Money is grouping!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: How many cents is a dime?

practice.prompt: A quarter is worth how many cents?

quickCheck.prompt: How many pennies equal one nickel?

k-word-add.title: Add Stories
k-word-add.einsteinIntro: Stories hide math! When things JOIN or MORE arrive — we ADD!

panels.speech: Mia has 3 stickers. She gets 2 more. Join them: 3 + 2 = 5!
Words like 'more', 'altogether', 'in all' whisper: ADD!

practice.prompt: Sam has 2 apples and gets 5 more. How many now?
Lia has 9 crayons and finds 1 more. Total?

k-word-sub.title: Take-Away Stories
k-word-sub.einsteinIntro: When some leave or we give away — we TAKE AWAY. Subtraction stories!

panels.speech: 8 balloons, 3 pop. How many left? 8 − 3 = 5!
Words like 'left', 'gave away', 'fewer' mean SUBTRACT!

practice.prompt: 9 birds, 2 fly away. How many left?

k-patterns-skip.title: Skip-Count by 2 & 5
k-patterns-skip.einsteinIntro: Skip-counting is hopping on the number line — by 2s or 5s. Boing!

panels.speech: By 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10… even numbers dancing!
By 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20… great for counting nickels!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: What comes after 6 when skip-counting by 2?

k-count-to-100-tens.title: Count by Tens to 100
k-count-to-100-tens.einsteinIntro: Tens are rocket boosters! 10, 20, 30… all the way to 100!

panels.speech: Skip-counting by 10s makes big numbers fly by!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: What comes after 40 when we count by 10s?

k-teen-decompose.title: Teens: 10 and Some More
k-teen-decompose.einsteinIntro: Every teen is a 10 plus some ones — like 13 is 10 + 3!

panels.speech: Teens are ten with extras hiding in the ones place!
16 = 10 + 6. The 1 in 16 means one ten!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Break 15 into a ten and ones.
steps: 15 has a 1 in the tens place

k-compare-teens.title: Compare Teen Numbers
k-compare-teens.einsteinIntro: Which teen is greater? Compare tens first — then ones!

panels.speech: Same tens? Peek at the ones! 14 vs 17 → 7 ones wins!
19 is greater than 12 because 9 ones > 2 ones.

practice.prompt: Which is greater, 14 or 15? (type the number)

k-doubles.title: Doubles Facts
k-doubles.einsteinIntro: Doubles are twin powers! 4+4, 6+6 — memorizing them is superhero speed!

panels.speech: A double means both addends are the same number!
5+5=10, 7+7=14, 8+8=16 — twin cosmic beams!

k-make-10-add.title: Make 10 to Add
k-make-10-add.einsteinIntro: When adding, zip to 10 first — then add the leftover ones. Relativity for addends!

panels.speech: 8 + 5: take 2 from 5 to make 10, then 3 left → 13!
Friends of 10 help every addition mission!

k-related-facts.title: Fact Families
k-related-facts.einsteinIntro: Add and subtract are siblings! 3+5=8, 5+3=8, 8−5=3 — one family!

panels.speech: If you know 2+6=8, you also know 8−6=2!
Three numbers dance together in a fact family.

k-time-half.title: Half Past the Hour
k-time-half.einsteinIntro: When the long hand points to 6, it's half past — halfway around the clock!

panels.speech: Long hand on 6 means 30 minutes — we say half past!
Short hand a little past 2 + long on 6 → half past 2.

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Long hand on 6, short past 4. Time?

k-weight-compare.title: Heavier or Lighter?
k-weight-compare.einsteinIntro: Balances and heft! Compare weight — feathers vs rocks, cosmic style!

panels.speech: Heavier sinks the scale down. Lighter floats up!
A watermelon is heavier than an apple — no relativity needed!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Feather vs book — which is heavier?

practice.prompt: On a balance, the heavier side…
Is an elephant heavier than a mouse? (yes/no)

k-coin-combos.title: Coin Combinations
k-coin-combos.einsteinIntro: Mix pennies, nickels, and dimes to make the same amount — money magic!

panels.speech: A nickel = 5 pennies. A dime = 10 pennies or 2 nickels!
15¢ could be a dime + nickel, or 3 nickels, or 15 pennies!

k-word-compare.title: How Many More?
k-word-compare.einsteinIntro: Compare stories ask: how many more? Find the difference — subtract!

panels.speech: 'How many more' means find the gap between two amounts!
Mia has 8, Leo has 5. How many more does Mia have? 8−5=3!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Sam has 9 stickers, Jo has 4. How many more does Sam have?

practice.prompt: 9 cats, 6 dogs. How many more cats?
10 red, 7 blue. How many more red?
5 birds, 2 nests. How many more birds?

k-word-put-together.title: Put-Together Stories
k-word-put-together.einsteinIntro: Some stories put groups together — that's addition adventure!

panels.speech: 'In all', 'altogether', 'total' → add the parts!
3 red rockets + 4 blue rockets = 7 rockets in all!

k-patterns-ab.title: AB Color Patterns
k-patterns-ab.einsteinIntro: Patterns repeat! Red-blue-red-blue is an AB pattern — predict the next!

panels.speech: A pattern has a repeating core. Spot the core, extend it!
Circle, square, circle, square… next is circle!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Pattern: star, circle, star, circle, star, ?

k-tally-pictograph.title: Tally Marks & Pictographs
k-tally-pictograph.einsteinIntro: Count votes with tally marks — and read picture graphs. Data detective!

panels.speech: Four tallies, then a diagonal fifth: four sticks become a bundle of 5!
In a pictograph, each picture often stands for 1 (or more)!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Tally of five (bundle) plus one more means?

k-shapes-3d.title: 3D Shape Friends
k-shapes-3d.einsteinIntro: Spheres, cubes, cones, cylinders — solid shapes you can hold!

panels.speech: Flat shapes are 2D. Solid shapes are 3D — they take up space!
A ball is a sphere. A die is a cube. An ice cream scoop sits on a cone!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: What 3D shape is a can of soup?
steps: Round sides, flat circles on ends
Soup can is like a cylinder

practice.prompt: A die (dice) is most like a…
How many faces on a cube? (number)

quickCheck.prompt: Can of soda is like a…

k-decompose-teens-add.title: Add with Teen Numbers
k-decompose-teens-add.einsteinIntro: Adding onto teens: 14+3 means keep the ten and add the ones!

panels.speech: 14 + 3 = 10 + (4+3) = 10 + 7 = 17. Decompose the teen!
Stay in the teens neighborhood — count on from the bigger number!

ages-7-8.label: Ages 7–8
ages-7-8.blurb: Place value & estimation, regrouping, mult/div ideas, fractions of sets, perimeter & elapsed time, graphs & multi-step WP — ~30 lessons.

units.title: Number Sense & Place Value
units.description: Understand how big numbers work — ones, tens, and hundreds!

units.title: Add & Subtract Fluency
units.description: Become a flash with addition and subtraction within 1000!

units.title: Multiply & Divide Ideas
units.description: Equal groups, arrays, and sharing — the secret of times tables!

units.title: Early Fractions
units.description: Halves, thirds, and fourths — pieces of the whole!

units.title: Measurement Basics
units.description: Length in inches/cm, time to 5 minutes, and making change!

units.title: Word Problem Heroes
units.description: 1–2 step add/sub stories and equal-groups adventures!

diagnostic.title: Cosmic Warm-Up
diagnostic.einsteinIntro: Ready for a quick warm-up across place value, ops, fractions, measurement, and stories? Just for fun!

questions.prompt: In 582, which digit is in the tens place?

ns-place-value-basics.title: Ones, Tens & Hundreds
ns-place-value-basics.einsteinIntro: Numbers are like cosmic building blocks! Ones, tens, and hundreds stack up to make ANY number. Let me show you the secret!

panels.speech: Look at 247. That's TWO hundreds, FOUR tens, and SEVEN ones!
The place of a digit tells you its POWER. A 4 in the tens place means 40 — not just 4!
So 247 = 200 + 40 + 7. That's expanded form — like exploding a number into parts!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Watch me build 135: 1 hundred + 3 tens + 5 ones. Easy as relativity!

practice.prompt: In 582, which digit is in the TENS place?
practice.hint: Tens are in the middle when you have hundreds-tens-ones.
practice.feedbackCorrect: Yes! The 8 is in the tens place — that's 80!

practice.prompt: What is the value of the 6 in 640?
practice.hint: The 6 is all the way on the left — that's the hundreds place!
practice.feedbackCorrect: Brilliant! 6 in the hundreds place means 600!
practice.feedbackWrong: Hmm… the 6 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 600.

practice.hint: Put the hundreds, tens, and ones digits together.
There's a zero in the tens place — so no tens!
practice.feedbackCorrect: Exactly! Zero tens means we skip the tens part: 300 + 5.

as-add-within-100.title: Adding Within 100
as-add-within-100.einsteinIntro: Addition is putting amounts together — like combining star energy! We'll add two-digit numbers and sometimes make a NEW ten. Exciting!

panels.speech: To add 37 + 25, line them up by place: ones under ones, tens under tens!
Ones first: 7 + 5 = 12. That's 1 ten and 2 ones! Write 2, carry the 1 ten.
Tens: 3 + 2 + the carried 1 = 6. So 37 + 25 = 62. Cosmic!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Let's add 48 + 36 together, step by step.

practice.feedbackWrong: Try ones first (3+1), then tens (2+4). You should get 64.

practice.feedbackCorrect: Fantastic! You carried the ten and got 85!
practice.feedbackWrong: Remember to carry: 7+8=15, so ones digit is 5 and carry 1 to tens.

practice.prompt: You have 46 stickers and get 37 more. How many now?
practice.feedbackWrong: Word problems are just stories about adding. 46 + 37 = 83.

md-equal-groups.title: Equal Groups
md-equal-groups.einsteinIntro: Multiplication is just FAST adding of equal groups! Like 3 bags with 4 stars each…

panels.speech: 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. We write that as 3 × 4 = 12!
An array is a neat rectangle of rows and columns. 2 rows of 5 is 2 × 5!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: 4 plates with 3 cookies each. How many cookies?

practice.prompt: 2 groups of 6. How many in all?

fr-halves-fourths.title: Halves & Fourths
fr-halves-fourths.einsteinIntro: Fractions are fair shares! Cut a whole into equal pieces and name one piece.

panels.speech: Cut a sandwich into 2 EQUAL parts — each is one-half, written 1/2!
Cut into 4 equal parts — each is one-fourth, or 1/4. Two fourths make a half!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: A chocolate bar split into 4 equal squares. You eat 1 square.

practice.prompt: A circle split into 2 equal parts. One part is…
practice.feedbackWrong: Two equal pieces mean each is 1/2.

practice.prompt: Which is bigger: 1/2 or 1/4 of the same pizza?
practice.hint: Fewer equal pieces means each piece is bigger.
practice.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Half is bigger than a fourth of the same pizza!
practice.feedbackWrong: A half is two fourths — so 1/2 > 1/4.

practice.prompt: How many fourths make one whole? (just the number)
practice.hint: Fourth means cut into 4 equal parts.
practice.feedbackWrong: It takes 4 fourths to rebuild the whole.

quickCheck.prompt: 2/4 of a bar is the same as…

ns-compare-numbers.title: Compare Numbers
ns-compare-numbers.einsteinIntro: Which number is greater? We compare place by place — hundreds first!

panels.speech: Compare 73 and 68. Look at tens first: 7 tens beats 6 tens, so 73 > 68!

as-sub-within-100.title: Subtract Within 100
as-sub-within-100.einsteinIntro: Subtraction is taking away — or finding the difference. Sometimes we borrow a ten. You've got this!

panels.speech: 52 − 18. Ones: 2 is smaller than 8, so borrow a ten! 12 − 8 = 4.
Tens left: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 34!

practice.hint: No borrowing needed. Ones then tens.

ns-rounding-intro.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10
ns-rounding-intro.einsteinIntro: Rounding is finding the nearest friendly ten — like teleporting to a landmark!

panels.speech: Look at the ones digit. 0–4 → round DOWN. 5–9 → round UP!
47 is closer to 50 than 40, so 47 rounds to 50. Bam!

md-arrays-div.title: Arrays & Sharing
md-arrays-div.einsteinIntro: Arrays are rows and columns. Sharing equally is division — fair cosmic splits!

panels.speech: 3 rows of 4 dots = 12. That's an array: 3 × 4 = 12!
Share 12 cookies with 3 friends equally → 12 ÷ 3 = 4 each!

practice.prompt: Share 15 into 3 equal groups. Each group?

fr-thirds-set.title: Thirds & Fractions of a Set
fr-thirds-set.einsteinIntro: Thirds cut a whole into THREE equal parts. Fractions can also claim part of a set!

panels.speech: 1/3 means one of three equal pieces. 2/3 means two of those pieces!
1/3 of 12 stars = 4 stars — because 12 ÷ 3 = 4!

practice.prompt: How many equal parts in thirds?

quickCheck.prompt: How many thirds make one whole?

ms-length-inch-cm.title: Inches & Centimeters
ms-length-inch-cm.einsteinIntro: Rulers measure length! Inches and centimeters are cosmic measuring sticks!

panels.speech: An inch is about a thumb tip. A centimeter is smaller — about a fingernail!
Line up at 0, then read the end. Don't start at 1 — start at ZERO!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: A crayon ends at 7 cm from 0.

practice.prompt: Which unit is shorter: 1 inch or 1 cm?
A pencil from 0 to 5 inches is how many inches?
About how long is a new crayon?

quickCheck.prompt: Object ends at 9 cm from 0. Length?

ms-time-5min.title: Time to 5 Minutes
ms-time-5min.einsteinIntro: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand. Skip-count around!

panels.speech: Long hand on 1 → 5 minutes. On 2 → 10 minutes. Skip-count by 5!
Short hand near 4, long hand on 6 → 4:30. Half past four!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Long hand on 3. How many minutes?

practice.prompt: Long hand on 2 means how many minutes?
Long hand on 4 → how many minutes?

ms-money-change.title: Money & Making Change
ms-money-change.einsteinIntro: Pay with coins and bills, then make change — like a shopkeeper hero!

panels.speech: Item costs 35¢. You pay 50¢. Change = 50 − 35 = 15¢!
Count up from the price to the money paid — that's change too!

wp-add-sub-1step.title: One-Step Add & Sub Stories
wp-add-sub-1step.einsteinIntro: One-step stories need one operation. Find the clue words — then compute!

panels.speech: Mia had 24 stickers and bought 15 more. 24 + 15 = 39. One step!
Leo had 50 points and lost 18. 50 − 18 = 32. Still one step!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Class has 28 kids. 6 more join. Total?

wp-add-sub-2step.title: Two-Step Add & Sub Stories
wp-add-sub-2step.einsteinIntro: Two-step stories need TWO moves — like a comic with a plot twist!

panels.speech: Start → do first action → then second. Write both steps!
Had 20. Bought 8. Gave away 5. (20+8)−5 = 23. Two steps!

wp-equal-groups.title: Equal-Groups Stories
wp-equal-groups.einsteinIntro: Equal-groups stories are multiplication or division in disguise!

panels.speech: 4 bags with 5 apples each → 4 × 5 = 20. Equal groups!
20 stickers shared by 4 kids → 20 ÷ 4 = 5 each. Fair share!

practice.prompt: 16 muffins for 4 trays equally. Each tray?

ns-estimate-sums.title: Estimate Sums
ns-estimate-sums.einsteinIntro: Round first, then add — estimation is a cosmic shortcut!

panels.speech: To estimate 48+31, round to 50+30=80 — close enough for a quick check!
Estimation asks 'about how many?' not the exact answer.

ns-round-hundreds.title: Round to Hundreds
ns-round-hundreds.einsteinIntro: Bigger place, bigger round! Look at tens to round to the nearest hundred.

panels.speech: To round to hundreds, peek at the tens digit. 5 or more → up!
350→400, 340→300. The tens digit decides!

practice.prompt: Which digit decides rounding to hundreds?

as-add-regroup.title: Add with Regrouping
as-add-regroup.einsteinIntro: When ones make 10 or more, trade for a ten — regrouping power!

panels.speech: 27+18: ones 7+8=15 → write 5, carry 1 ten!
Regrouping keeps place value honest across columns.

as-sub-regroup.title: Subtract with Regrouping
as-sub-regroup.einsteinIntro: Not enough ones? Borrow a ten — regrouping for subtraction!

panels.speech: Borrowing is just regrouping a ten into 10 ones.

md-facts-2-5-10.title: Facts: 2s, 5s, 10s
md-facts-2-5-10.einsteinIntro: Skip-count to learn multiplication facts for 2, 5, and 10!

panels.speech: 5×4 means 4 jumps of 5: 5,10,15,20!
×10 just tacks on a zero: 7×10=70. Cosmic cheat code!

md-quotative.title: Division: How Many Groups?
md-quotative.einsteinIntro: Quotative division asks: how many groups of size n fit inside a total?

panels.speech: 12 ÷ 3 as 'how many groups of 3 in 12?' → 4 groups!
Sharing (partitive) vs grouping (quotative) — both are division!

practice.prompt: 'How many teams of 4 from 12 kids?' is…

fr-set-of.title: Fraction of a Set
fr-set-of.einsteinIntro: Find 1/2 of 8, 1/4 of 12 — split the set into equal shares!

panels.speech: 1/3 of a set means split into 3 equal groups, take one group!

fr-unit-fractions.title: Unit Fractions
fr-unit-fractions.einsteinIntro: Unit fractions have 1 on top: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 — one equal piece!

panels.speech: A unit fraction names one piece of a whole split equally.
1/4 is smaller than 1/2 because pieces are tinier when more splits!

ms-perimeter.title: Perimeter Paths
ms-perimeter.einsteinIntro: Perimeter is the fence around a shape — add all the side lengths!

panels.speech: Walk the outline: side+side+side+side = perimeter!
Rectangle 3 by 5: 3+5+3+5=16 units around.

ms-elapsed-time.title: Elapsed Time
ms-elapsed-time.einsteinIntro: How much time passed? From start to end — elapsed time mission!

panels.speech: From 2:00 to 2:30 is 30 minutes elapsed.
Count forward on the clock from start until end!

ms-bar-graph.title: Read Bar Graphs
ms-bar-graph.einsteinIntro: Bars show amounts! Read the scale and compare heights — data hero!

panels.speech: A bar graph uses bar height to show quantity.
Taller bar = more. Check the axis numbers carefully!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Bar for cats at 4, dogs at 6. How many more dogs?

practice.prompt: Cats 3, birds 7. How many more birds?

wp-multi-step.title: Multi-Step Word Problems
wp-multi-step.einsteinIntro: Some stories need two moves — add then subtract, or multiply then add!

panels.speech: Underline the question. Do step 1, then step 2. Check!
Had 10, found 4, gave away 3: 10+4=14, 14−3=11.

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: Lia had 15. Bought 6 more. Gave 4 away. Now?

wp-money-stories.title: Money Story Problems
wp-money-stories.einsteinIntro: Buy, save, make change — money word problems with cents!

panels.speech: Cost and pay → change is subtract. Two items → add costs first!
Snack 40¢ + juice 25¢ = 65¢. Pay 100¢ → change 35¢.

md-multiply-stories.title: Equal-Groups Stories
md-multiply-stories.einsteinIntro: Word problems with equal groups → multiply to find the total!

panels.speech: '4 bags with 6 apples each' → 4×6=24 apples!
Each, every, groups of — multiplication clues!

as-add-fluency.title: Addition Fluency within 100
as-add-fluency.einsteinIntro: Practice speedy adds — with and without regrouping — until it feels automatic!

panels.speech: Warm up with friendly numbers, then mix in regrouping challenges!
Check with estimation: 47+36 should be about 80.

ages-9-10.label: Ages 9–10
ages-9-10.blurb: Multi-digit ops, factors/primes, fractions & mixed numbers, decimal ops, area/volume, coordinates & multi-step WP — ~30 lessons.

units.title: Multi-Digit Power
units.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide with bigger numbers!

units.title: Factor Force
units.description: Factors, multiples, and light order of operations!

units.title: Fraction Universe
units.description: Equivalence, compare, add same denominators, mixed numbers!

units.title: Decimals, Area & Volume
units.description: Decimal place value, compare, area, and volume word problems!

diagnostic.title: Galaxy Warm-Up
diagnostic.einsteinIntro: Quick warm-up across multi-digit ops, factors, fractions, decimals, and area — cosmic style!

g4-multi-add.title: Multi-Digit Addition
g4-multi-add.einsteinIntro: Big numbers, same rules! Line up places, add ones first, carry the tens — KAPOW!

panels.speech: Add 1,456 + 378. Line up ones under ones. Start from the RIGHT!
Ones: 6+8=14 → write 4, carry 1. Keep carrying through tens, hundreds…
Result: 1,834. Place value is your superpower!

practice.prompt: A library has 1,250 books and gets 375 more. Total?

g4-multi-sub.title: Multi-Digit Subtraction
g4-multi-sub.einsteinIntro: Subtraction with big numbers — borrow across places when you need to!

panels.speech: 5,000 − 1,234. Lots of zeros? Borrow carefully across!
Think: 5,000 − 1,000 = 4,000, then subtract the leftover 234 → 3,766.

g4-factors-intro.title: Factors Intro
g4-factors-intro.einsteinIntro: Factors are numbers that multiply to make another number — the secret ingredients!

panels.speech: Factors of 12: 1×12, 2×6, 3×4. So factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12!
A prime number has ONLY two factors: 1 and itself. Like 7!

practice.hint: Does it divide 15 with no leftover?

quickCheck.prompt: Which number is a factor of 18?

g4-frac-equiv.title: Equivalent Fractions
g4-frac-equiv.einsteinIntro: Same amount, different costume! 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 — equivalent fractions!

panels.speech: Multiply top AND bottom by the same number: 1/2 × 2/2 = 2/4.
Simplify by dividing top and bottom by a common factor: 4/8 ÷ 4/4 = 1/2.

g4-frac-compare.title: Compare Fractions
g4-frac-compare.einsteinIntro: Who wins the fraction showdown? Same denominator — bigger top wins. Same numerator — smaller bottom wins!

panels.speech: 3/8 vs 5/8: same size pieces, so 5 pieces beat 3. 5/8 > 3/8!
1/3 vs 1/5: same top. Thirds are bigger slices than fifths → 1/3 > 1/5!

practice.hint: Same numerator; smaller denominator is bigger.

practice.prompt: Which is bigger, 3/8 or 7/8? Type it like 7/8

quickCheck.prompt: Order least to greatest: 1/2, 1/5, 1/3. Which is least?

g4-decimals-area.title: Decimals & Area
g4-decimals-area.einsteinIntro: Decimals are fractions in disguise — 0.3 means 3 tenths! And area = length × width.

panels.speech: 0.7 = 7/10. The first digit after the point is tenths; next is hundredths.
A rectangle 5 by 3 has area 5 × 3 = 15 square units. Cover the comic panel!

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: What is 0.4 as a fraction? Area of 6×4?

practice.prompt: 0.25 as a fraction in lowest terms?

g4-multi-mult.title: Multi-Digit Multiplication Ideas
g4-multi-mult.einsteinIntro: Multiply like a superhero: break numbers apart, multiply parts, then add — POW!

panels.speech: Stack the numbers, multiply ones, then tens — keep places lined up!

g4-multi-div.title: Division Concepts
g4-multi-div.einsteinIntro: Division asks: how many equal groups? Or how many in each group?

panels.speech: 84 ÷ 4 means share 84 into 4 equal groups — or how many 4s fit in 84!
Think multiply backwards: 4 × ? = 84. If 4 × 20 = 80, remainder 4 → 21!

g4-factors-multiples.title: Factors & Multiples Deep Dive
g4-factors-multiples.einsteinIntro: Factors build a number. Multiples are that number's skip-count trail!

panels.speech: Factors of 12: 1,2,3,4,6,12. Multiples of 4: 4,8,12,16…
Every multiple of 6 is also a multiple of 2 and 3 — factor friends!

practice.prompt: List how many factors 9 has (count them).

g4-order-ops.title: Order of Operations (Light)
g4-order-ops.einsteinIntro: When expressions get busy, order matters! Parentheses first, then ×÷, then +−.

panels.speech: Do what's in ( ) first. Then multiply/divide left to right. Then add/subtract!
2 + 3 × 4 = 2 + 12 = 14 — NOT 20. Multiplication before addition!

g4-frac-add-same.title: Add & Subtract Fractions (Same Denominator)
g4-frac-add-same.einsteinIntro: Same denominator? Add or subtract the numerators — keep the denominator!

panels.speech: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7. Bottom stays 7; tops add: 2+3=5!
5/8 − 2/8 = 3/8. Same rule — subtract numerators only!

g4-mixed-intro.title: Mixed Numbers Intro
g4-mixed-intro.einsteinIntro: A mixed number is a whole number PLUS a fraction — like 2 1/3!

panels.speech: 7/3 = 2 1/3 because 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1.
2 1/4 means 2 wholes and 1/4 more. Improper ↔ mixed are twins!

practice.prompt: How many wholes in 11/5? (just the whole number)

g4-decimal-pv.title: Decimal Place Value
g4-decimal-pv.einsteinIntro: Decimals extend place value to the right of the point — tenths, hundredths!

panels.speech: In 0.46: 4 is tenths (4/10), 6 is hundredths (6/100).
0.5 = 5/10 = one half. Decimals and fractions are cosmic cousins!

practice.prompt: In 0.82, the 8 is in the _____ place.
In 3.14, digit in hundredths? (just the digit)

g4-decimal-compare.title: Compare Decimals
g4-decimal-compare.einsteinIntro: Line up the decimal points and compare place by place — left to right!

panels.speech: Compare 0.45 and 0.5: think 0.50 vs 0.45 → 0.5 is greater!
Annex zeros: 0.4 = 0.40. Same length makes comparing fair!

practice.prompt: Order: write the smaller of 0.6 and 0.58

g4-volume-wp.title: Area & Volume Word Problems
g4-volume-wp.einsteinIntro: Area covers flat space. Volume fills 3D boxes — length × width × height!

panels.speech: Area of a 6×4 rectangle = 24 square units. Cover the floor!
Volume of a 2×3×4 box = 24 cubic units. Fill the box!

practice.prompt: A garden is 10 m by 4 m. Area?

g4-long-mult.title: Long Multiplication Ideas
g4-long-mult.einsteinIntro: Break apart factors: 23×4 = (20×4)+(3×4). Partial products to the rescue!

panels.speech: Multiply ones, then tens — add the partial products!

g4-long-div.title: Long Division Ideas
g4-long-div.einsteinIntro: Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — the long division loop!

panels.speech: 84÷3: how many 3s in 8? 2… then bring down 4…
Check with multiplication: quotient × divisor should rebuild the dividend!

g4-primes.title: Primes & Composites
g4-primes.einsteinIntro: Primes have exactly two factors: 1 and themselves. Composites have more!

panels.speech: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 are primes. 4, 6, 8, 9 are composites.
1 is neither prime nor composite — a special cosmic loner!

practice.prompt: Number of factors in a prime?

g4-order-ops-deep.title: Order of Ops Practice
g4-order-ops-deep.einsteinIntro: PEMDAS power-up: parentheses, then ×÷ left to right, then +−!

panels.speech: Do 3+(2×4) — multiply inside first → 3+8=11, not 20!
Left to right for same-level ops: 12÷3×2 = 4×2 = 8.

g4-frac-times-whole.title: Fraction × Whole
g4-frac-times-whole.einsteinIntro: 1/3 of 12 is 12×(1/3)=4. Multiply numerator by the whole, keep denominator!

panels.speech: a/b × n = (a×n)/b. Or think: split into b groups, take a of them.
2/5 × 10 = 20/5 = 4. Simplify when you can!

g4-mixed-add.title: Add Mixed Numbers (Like Denoms)
g4-mixed-add.einsteinIntro: Add wholes, add fractions — regroup if the fraction part is improper!

panels.speech: 1 2/5 + 2 1/5 = 3 3/5. Same denominators make it smooth!
If fraction ≥1, regroup: 3 5/4 → 4 1/4.

g4-decimal-add.title: Add Decimals
g4-decimal-add.einsteinIntro: Line up the decimal points — tenths under tenths — then add!

panels.speech: Keep the decimal point in the sum aligned!

g4-decimal-sub.title: Subtract Decimals
g4-decimal-sub.einsteinIntro: Align decimals, subtract like whole numbers — borrow carefully!

panels.speech: 0.90 − 0.35 = 0.55. Tenths and hundredths stay in their lanes!
Annex zeros if helpful: 0.5 = 0.50.

g4-volume-rect.title: Rectangular Prism Volume
g4-volume-rect.einsteinIntro: Volume = length × width × height — unit cubes packed inside!

panels.speech: A 3×2×4 prism holds 24 unit cubes. V=l×w×h!
Count layers: each layer is l×w cubes, times height layers.

g4-coord-plane.title: Coordinate Plane Intro
g4-coord-plane.einsteinIntro: Ordered pairs (x,y): x right/left, y up/down from the origin!

panels.speech: Origin is (0,0). First number = x (horizontal), second = y (vertical).
(3,2) means right 3, up 2. Plot like a cosmic treasure map!

g4-multi-step-wp.title: Multi-Step Problem Solving
g4-multi-step-wp.einsteinIntro: Read, plan, solve, check — multi-step word problems for grade 4–5 heroes!

panels.speech: Find hidden steps: sometimes multiply, then subtract leftovers.
A bakery sells 4 boxes of 6, then 5 more singles → 4×6+5=29.

workedExample.title: Worked Example
workedExample.speech: 3 packs of 8 stickers, give away 5. Left?

g4-frac-sub-same.title: Subtract Fractions (Same Denom)
g4-frac-sub-same.einsteinIntro: Same denominator? Subtract numerators, keep the bottom number!

panels.speech: 5/8 − 2/8 = 3/8. Denominator stays; numerators subtract!
Simplify if you can: 4/6 − 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.

practice.prompt: Keep the _____ when subtracting like fractions.

g4-area-rect.title: Area of Rectangles
g4-area-rect.einsteinIntro: Area = length × width — square units covering the inside!

panels.speech: A 6×4 rectangle has area 24 square units.
Area is inside; perimeter is around — don't mix them up!

g4-factors-deep.title: Factor Pairs Deep Dive
g4-factors-deep.einsteinIntro: List factor pairs systematically — don't miss any cosmic partners!

panels.speech: For 24: 1×24, 2×12, 3×8, 4×6 — stop when factors repeat!
A number is divisible by a factor if division has no remainder.

g4-mixed-sub.title: Subtract Mixed Numbers (Light)
g4-mixed-sub.einsteinIntro: Subtract wholes and like fractions — borrow a whole if needed!

panels.speech: 3 1/4 − 1 2/4: not enough fourths → borrow → 2 5/4 − 1 2/4 = 1 3/4.
Same denominators keep the cosmic gears meshing smoothly.
